title: Do sEMG Foundation Models Improve Cross-Subject Generalisation?
abstract: arXiv:2611.08199v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: sEMG Foundation Models aim to learn general purpose representations over diverse subjects and recording conditions that boost performance on a variety of downstream tasks. However, existing evaluations make it difficult to discern whether pretraining alone is sufficient to combat the cross-subject overfitting which makes machine learning on sEMG so challenging. We conduct a systematic evaluation of three sEMG foundation models across three gesture classification datasets under both intra-session and inter-subject splits, using three fine-tuning strategies designed to isolate the contribution of pretraining. We find that pretraining boosts performance when train and test samples are drawn from the same recording session, but this benefit largely disappears under inter-subject evaluation. In low subject count datasets, pretraining provides little to no benefit and classical ML baselines match or exceed foundation model performance.

translated_title: sEMG基础模型能否提升跨受试者泛化能力？
translated_abstract: 表面肌电信号基础模型旨在学习跨多样受试者和记录条件的通用表示，以提升各种下游任务的性能。然而，现有评估难以辨别仅靠预训练是否足以克服跨受试者过拟合问题——这正是使sEMG机器学习如此具有挑战性的关键。我们对三个sEMG基础模型在三个手势分类数据集上进行了系统评估，采用会话内和跨受试者两种数据划分方式，并使用三种微调策略来隔离预训练本身的贡献。我们发现，当训练和测试样本来自同一记录会话时，预训练确实能提升性能，但在跨受试者评估下这种优势基本消失。在受试者数量较少的数据集中，预训练几乎无益，经典机器学习基线可匹敌甚至超越基础模型的性能。
tldr: 本研究通过系统评估发现，sEMG基础模型的预训练优势仅在会话内评估中显著，在跨受试者泛化场景下基本消失，且在小规模受试者数据集上经典机器学习基线可匹敌甚至超越基础模型。
en_tdlr: This systematic evaluation reveals that the benefits of pretraining in sEMG foundation models largely disappear under cross-subject generalization, with classical ML baselines matching or exceeding foundation model performance on low subject-count datasets.
